title: STUDY TOPIC Spiritual formation [the process of becoming like Jesus] part 4
devotional:
How are we to understand the image of God? (cont’d)

1. The image of God explains God’s purpose and our function.

When we read the Genesis account of creation we are inclined to think more about the ‘from’ of creation rather than the ‘for’ The Hebrew word ‘bara,’ create is more concerned about the ‘for,’ the purpose, the reason. God made us in his image so we can become like Jesus. In the New Testament Jesus is referred to as the Image of God.

Colossians 1:15

‘’He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation.’’

2 Corinthians 4:4

‘’In whose case the god of this world has blinded the minds of the unbelieving so that they might not see the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.’’

Hebrews 1:3

‘’And He is the radiance of His glory and the exact representation of His nature, and upholds all things by the word of His power. When He had made purification of sins, He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high,

Christ as the image of God, is a reflection of God that demonstrates God’s intentions for all humanity. Christ illustrates God’s purposes and goals for humanity, Christ demonstrates who people can be. You could say that being created in the image of God gives us the opportunity to reflect Jesus’ relationship with His father and with others. The image of God in you, gives you the potential of having an intimate relationship with God. The image of God expresses God’s ultimate desire for our lives and our greatest need.

2. A proper understanding of the image of God will determine how we treat others.

If God created humans in His image, and every life has value, then we cannot ignore those trapped in poverty, trafficking, or homelessness. We cannot ignore the widow or the orphan who bears the image of God. As image bearers of God—protector of strangers and helper of the fatherless and the widow (Ps. 146:9)

Has God not told us? …

“Open your hand willingly to your poor and needy brother in your land” (Deut. 15:11).

“Speak up for those who have no voice, for the justice of all who are dispossessed. Speak up, judge righteously, and defend the cause of the oppressed and needy” (Prov. 31:8-9).

“Pursue justice. Correct the oppressor. Defend the rights of the fatherless. Plead the widow’s cause” (Isa. 1:17).

Jesus taught that our response to the least of this world is in some measure an indication of the validity of the relationship with profess to have with Him. (See Matt. 25:35-45.

“I see Jesus in every human being. I say to myself, this is hungry Jesus, I must feed him. This is sick Jesus, I must look after Him. This one has leprosy or gangrene; I must wash him and tend to him. I serve because I love Jesus.”―Mother Teresa

Seeing others as people created in the image of God will cause you to treat them with dignity and respect. When others see you as someone created in the image of God they will treat you with dignity and respect.

So often the church has abandoned this perspective. We allow people’s sin and failure to define them. The best way to understand another person’ sinfulness and the effect it has on their lives, is to firstly view them as people made in the image of God. It is important that we understand that no one’s sin has any ability to devalue them. For example if you were to get a coin with the kings head on it, if the image of the kings head was faded, our even difficult to make out, would that mean that particular coin had lost some of it’s value? No of course not.

Sin may diminish or fade the image of God in someone, but it will never eradicate it, or make that person less valuable. When Jesus looked upon the crowds he had compassion on them and seen them as sheep without a shepherd. Matthew 9:36. Not as lost sinners who deserved to be condemned.

According to James 3:9 to curse a person who is made in the image of God is wrong. Cursing people is the same as cursing God. When we damage and dishonour people we are doing the same to God. Conversely, treating people well honours God. If dishonouring and mistreating people is an attack on God it is not surprising that Satan under the guise of the serpent attacked and deceived Adam and Eve.

If we were to take a step back, and think about people in our lives who have caused us pain... No matter how we feel about these people, their wrong treatment of you/me doest not make them any less created in the image of God.
prayer: Father thank you a persons sin cannot rob them of value.
